title: Input-port node created before child-membership filter -> orphan port nodes (asymmetric with output-port handling)
description: In handleDrillIntoSubmodel, the input-port construction creates a SUBMODEL_PORT node for every parent source (line 120) and only afterwards filters which child edges to draw with `if (!childIds.has(childId)) continue` (line 127). The output-port construction does the opposite: it applies the membership filter during grouping (line 146 `if (!childIds.has(childId)) continue`) and additionally requires `e.sourceHandle` (line 141), so a target with no valid in-submodel children never enters `outputsByTarget` and no orphan output port is created. Because of this asymmetry, any parent edge that targets the submodel node but resolves to a childId not present in the submodel (e.g. `targetHandle` missing -> childId becomes the sentinel `"__unconnected__"`, line 111; or a stale `in__<id>` handle after edit/dissolve/re-create cycles) still produces an input port node (`port_in__<srcId>`) with zero connecting edges. That orphan node is passed to getLayoutedElements and rendered with no edges. There is no later pruning of edge-less port nodes.
evidence: Input branch: inputsBySource groups e.source -> childIds (including "__unconnected__" sentinel). For each srcId it unconditionally `newNodes.push(validateReactFlowNode({id: port_in__<srcId>, ...}))` (120-125), THEN loops children with `if (!childIds.has(childId)) continue` (126-127). So a source whose only target child is "__unconnected__" (or any non-member id) yields a port node but no edge. Output branch filters first (146 `if (!childIds.has(childId)) continue` before adding to outputsByTarget), so no equivalent orphan output port is ever created. Symmetric fix would skip creating the input port when none of its targetChildIds are in childIds.
